status: frozen synthetic holdout for BNK-PDF-1 G12; sealed and committed before the product was run on any of its files
question: G10's statements did not exercise G8's rule for a DR written after its amount or its rule for a date written as touching runs, nor G10's own rules for a clip path traced back to its start; and G10's eligibility was wrong for two positives and its decision story. On statements from two writers applications use to draw their own statements, Apache PDFBox and jsPDF with autoTable, checked before the seal by the eligibility check G11 built, does bank-statement-native-1 complete every eligible positive with no false automatic approval, and which of G8's and G10's rules does each statement need?

producers: Apache PDFBox 3.0.5 with ICU4J 76.1: a Java application drawing its own table, each cell line placed by the program and written with one showText; Arabic shaped into presentation forms and ordered by ICU4J, as PDFBox does neither; one Arabic statement written run by run in its bidi order, so that a date in Arabic-Indic digits is five touching texts; one statement's overdrawn balances with DR written in its own slot after the amount; one statement's cells each clipped by a path traced back to its start and not closed

jsPDF 4.2.1 with jspdf-autotable 5.0.8: a web application's statement, each page's letterhead by doc.text and its table by autoTable in its striped, grid or plain theme; Arabic shaped and ordered by jsPDF itself, in its right-to-left mode; a page laid out landscape by its own width and height
fonts: Times-Roman and Courier, the PDF standard fonts, not embedded

PDFBox's copies of the Fontsource fonts without the liga and clig features, which PDFBox 3 would otherwise apply and write without their letters, and, for the Arabic fonts, without the code points that share a glyph with an Arabic letter but name another letter
geometry: a full grid of stroked cells
a full grid with a filled heading
autoTable's striped rows and coloured heading
descriptions wrapping over two or three lines in English and Arabic
every cell's text clipped to its cell
the period's dates with their segments reversed in a right-to-left account line when the bidi algorithm orders them so

A contractor's cheque presented six days after it was written; a tenant's cheque returned unpaid with the bank's fee, not yet booked; two months' rent in one transfer against two receipts under one reference; a tenant paying short of the rent; a maintenance payment without its reference on the statement, booked a day later; an electricity bill valued before the period and a rent valued after it; the bank's monthly fee; two equal cash deposits on one day against two equal receipts; a security deposit refunded but booked as a receipt; a cheque issued and not yet presented; a cheque deposited on the last day and not yet credited; a water bill paid twice under one bill number against one entry; accounts falling overdrawn or overdrawn from the start, with DR printed in proportional, monospaced and Arabic-Indic type

independence.author: The same assistant wrote the product, the foundation, the oracle, the G6, G8, G9 and G10 holdouts, the G6, G7, G8 and G10 fixes, the G11 eligibility check and this holdout, and knew the reader's rules when designing the stories. A DR in its own slot, a date as touching runs and a clip path traced back to its start are in the stories because G10's statements did not exercise the rules added for them; they are what applications that draw their own statements write, and how the product reads them is not known before the run. This is not a blind holdout: the stories and the writers are new to the product, the author is not.
independence.oracle: audit/bank-statement-foundation/oracle.py, unchanged: it reads the printed lines in the facts, the cashbook CSV and the contract, never recipe or intent, and imports nothing from the generator or the product. expected.py only runs it story by story with each story's own period.
independence.verifier: pdfminer.six, a PDF reader unrelated to the product's pdf.js, finds every printed line of the facts on its own row with all its values, and every description's words in order across the rows the writer wraps it over, Arabic in reading order glyph by glyph (verify.py, with its own self-test of 36 planted changes and 2 changed XLSX cashbooks).
independence.eligibility: audit/bank-statement-eligibility/eligibility.py, run on the frozen PDFs before the seal with MuPDF and the raw content streams, never the product: every refusal the reader declares that a statement could fall into, and the decision story's case and outstanding item. Its report, ELIGIBILITY.json, is sealed and bound to the PDF hashes.
independence.generator: stories.py is a sixth lineage: a property manager's collection account driven by a xoshiro128** generator seeded through SplitMix32; nothing is imported from the foundation's stories.mjs or from the G6, G8, G9 or G10 holdouts.
independence.drafts: While the stories and writers were drafted, their PDFs were read only with pdfminer.six, Poppler's pdftotext, pdfinfo and pdftoppm, MuPDF and the eligibility check, never with the product's reader.
independence.notTuned: The product was not run on these files, and no product code changed, between the start of G12 and the seal.

eligibility.why: Every statement stays inside the contract: its headings, labels, footer, line kinds, number and date formats and matching policy. The writer, font, table style, geometry, period, furniture and story are what the contract leaves open. The eligibility check found nothing in any of the twelve statements that the reader declares a reason to refuse (ELIGIBILITY.json), so a refusal of a positive is not a correct one.
eligibility.draftFindings: In the first drafts the eligibility check found every glyph of Q08, Q10 and Q11 inside a drawing: autoTable's grid theme fills each body cell white and strokes its border in one operation (re ... B), and the reader takes a shape filled and stroked at once as a drawing over the text inside it and refuses the page, a refusal it declares. Those statements were not declared positive with that style: their cells are drawn stroked only, as autoTable does when a cell has no fill colour, and the finding is reported with G12 as a question for the product, not measured by this holdout.

browserDecision.why: The browser run accepts the first acceptable case of one story and the export checker's self-test alters that story's workbook. Q01 has a case the page accepts (date-gap) and items outstanding, so every alteration has a target (DEV-51, DEV-55); ELIGIBILITY.json checks it. If the product refuses Q01, the next of Q08 (date-gap, items outstanding) and Q04 (amount-date-suggestion, an item outstanding) it does not refuse is decided.

attribution.what: After the first run, the same package is run on the product before G8's fixes and recorded beside it, so that each completed positive says whether it needed G8's rules (DEV-52). It is a diagnostic, not a second result.

rules: rectangle traced back to its start
ablation.what: After the first run, on the commit it ran on, each rule G8 and G10 added is switched off in a private copy of the product, one at a time, and the package run again: a positive that completes with every rule and not with one off needed it. The statements written to need a rule are Q03 (DR after its amount), Q02 (date runs joined), Q01 (rectangle traced back to its start) and Q03 (typed cashbook amounts); whether they need it is what the ablation measures. It is a diagnostic, not a second result.

measures.reading: Every printed line read from the PDF equals the facts: kind, page, dates, reference, amounts, balances; descriptions and continuation text after NFKC and whitespace normalisation.
measures.result: The matching result, in the facts' keys, equals EXPECTED.json: automatic pairs, review groups with their reasons, both outstanding sides, timing, and held statements with their counts.
measures.capacity: Eligible positives whose result equals EXPECTED.json from upload through matching, save, restore and Excel in the browser.
measures.falseAutomatic: Automatic pairs that EXPECTED.json does not hold, over all twelve statements. Must be zero.
measures.held: A held statement is held whole, with the oracle's status, and nothing in it approved, suggested or called outstanding.
measures.refusal: A positive the product refuses, or holds without the oracle holding it, is a failed positive, never a correct abstention.

afterRun: Results are recorded as they come, with the commit they ran on. A fix made after seeing them turns this set into regression for that fix; a new claim of generalisation needs a new holdout.
